label: Hidden evaluation rubric: Contributor 01 and Project Lantern

themes.name: Diagnosis and proposal
themes.criterion: Conclude that Contributor 01 connected demand peaks with overlapping defrost starts, while treating door activity as a competing explanation, and proposed a guarded 12-minute staggering test rather than asserting proven causality.
themes.pitfall: Saying Contributor 01 proved defrost overlap caused the peaks or originated the underlying incident report.

themes.name: Analysis tooling and timestamp correction
themes.criterion: Conclude that Contributor 01 built the parser, overlap detector, and simulator, then acknowledged and corrected an offset/DST assumption after Contributor 07 identified it; the corrected analysis still supported investigating overlap.
themes.pitfall: Omitting the defect, treating it as fatal to all findings, or crediting Contributor 01 with discovering it unaided.

themes.name: Pilot design and governance
themes.criterion: Conclude that Contributor 01 drafted a supervised, bounded pilot with stop conditions and an excluded ambiguous interval, while operations and controls contributors set staffing, approval, and safety constraints.
themes.pitfall: Portraying Contributor 01 as sole owner of the pilot or claiming the plan authorised autonomous control.

themes.name: Recommendation-mode implementation
themes.criterion: Conclude that Contributor 01 implemented read-only scheduling recommendations, eligibility checks, delay visibility, audit logging, operator hold, rejection stopping, and tests; it did not submit controller commands automatically.
themes.pitfall: Calling the implementation an autonomous scheduler or omitting review-driven safety changes.

themes.name: Observed first-site result
themes.criterion: Report that four supervised Freezer B nights reduced matched eligible overlaps from 11 to 3 and had an observed maximum-demand difference of 38 kW, with no measurable energy change or recorded safety event.
themes.pitfall: Calling 38 kW a proven or annualised saving, generalising from four nights, or ignoring operator intervention.

themes.name: Causality and shared ownership
themes.criterion: Recognise that lower door-open time confounded two nights and that Contributor 01 explicitly credited operations, Contributor 07, and Contributor 03; the outcome was shared rather than solely attributable.
themes.pitfall: Repeating informal praise as evidence that Contributor 01 personally delivered the entire outcome.

themes.name: Second-site constraint
themes.criterion: Conclude that Chiller C's R4 gateway incompatibility blocked the planned screen-assisted workflow; only two manual nights occurred, one with too few eligible cycles, and Contributor 01 declined to build an undocumented adapter because of unit risk.
themes.pitfall: Calling the pause a failed safety test, claiming deployment occurred, or assuming Contributor 01 caused the vendor constraint.

themes.name: Documentation and terminology
themes.criterion: Conclude that Contributor 01 authored the operating guide and distinguished supported from unsupported controllers, while Contributor 04 added screenshots and corrected language to reflect operator confirmation rather than autonomous approval.
themes.pitfall: Crediting Contributor 01 with every guide detail or describing documentation as proof of broad adoption.

themes.name: Responsible outcome framing
themes.criterion: Conclude that Contributor 01 sought cautious reporting: observed 38 kW difference, unchanged energy, no annualisation; tariff benefit remained unknown.
themes.pitfall: Converting the trial observation into a financial or energy-saving claim.

themes.name: Later safeguard work
themes.criterion: Conclude that Contributor 01 fixed stale recommendations after telemetry loss with a 30-second disconnected state and fresh recalculation; this resolved that display hazard but not the R4 issue.
themes.pitfall: Omitting the later corrective work or claiming it removed all deployment blockers.

themes.name: Follow-up adoption and unresolved scale
themes.criterion: Through 2028-06-30, conclude that Freezer B saw intermittent selected-night use, Chiller C had no supported deployment, and there was no fleet rollout or portfolio-wide measurement; incomplete logs and pending controller replacement leave adoption and impact uncertain.
themes.pitfall: Equating occasional reported use with general adoption, treating delay as definite failure, or using the post-horizon controller approval as an in-scope outcome.

themes.name: Evidence boundaries
themes.criterion: Keep the unavailable vendor appendix out of factual support and exclude the 2028-07-09 controller decision from conclusions bounded by the follow-up horizon.
themes.pitfall: Relying on inaccessible material or incorporating chat:017 into the through-horizon answer.

author_note: This is a wholly synthetic case. Records are concise reconstructions rather than complete workplace archives; meter precision, seasonal variation, billing consequences, exact later usage, and counterfactual causality remain deliberately unresolved.
